questions.text: Compare Design A (1:10 WFR, equal windows on 4 sides) and Design B (1:10 WFR, windows only on North and South facades). Which is preferred for the Philippines?

options.text: Design A; it provides uniform light from all directions and maximizes daylighting flexibility.
Design B; it minimizes heat gain by eliminating East/West glazing.
Design A; it is easier to comply with code and simplifies window scheduling documentation.
Design B; but it is non-compliant because it lacks East/West light required by the code.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 Section 808 supports the 10% window-opening minimum. The 2.5x daylight-depth rule and tropical facade orientation are design heuristics; use them only when the question frames them as design guidance rather than code.
questions.explanation: Uniform light from all sides includes uncontrollable heat gain from the West. Both have the same WFR (1:10), so both comply with the minimum area requirement. Code does not require windows on all sides; it only requires a total area relative to the floor. Design B follows passive cooling principles by placing windows on the North/South sides, which are easier to shade, while avoiding the harsh East/West solar heat gain. Passive design favors North-South orientation for glazing in the Philippines.
